answer: Latency Ladder: each identity accrues a public “jetty” of verified wait-time; transactions are ordered only after that identity’s oldest unspent slot clears. A sparrow-sized identity must wait a full epoch before its first action settles; parallel identities don’t shorten the queue because each canyons through its own delayed lane. An attacker running N identities pays N × epoch latency plus the compute cost of maintaining idle agent processes, so fake accounts become slower and costlier than the real work they mimic.
